- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or neutral, model often overestimates; apply downward bias, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–3% after 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong upward bias in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) — reduce slope or apply linear decay to forecast curve.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often ignores it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- When sentiment history includes 0.5 or higher, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 3 days, model is likely overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.
